judgements.justification: The one wrong claim on A's side (KUr5's 'strong theoretical guarantee') was praise, not criticism; no score fell on a wrong claim.

B's AC chose an oral although no reviewer rated above 8, on a personal reading ('I have gone through the paper by myself'), personal taste for 'a simple idea that works' and an impact claim no reviewer made.
B's Reviewer_Xxt6 gave 8 after 2 hours, listed no weakness and called Fig. 1 'inspiring'; B's reviews mostly restate the paper's claims and lifted B's mean to 7.75.
Both forums received the same core rebuttal content; no flaw was disclosed to one committee only.
Neither committee learned of a substantive flaw it then ignored; the gradient-series problem and the shortcut-only gap went unseen as flaws on both sides.
In B, Reviewer_f6JJ and Reviewer_oG66 raised scores after the response, while A's KUr5 kept 7 and no A score moved.
Only A questioned why a Fourier series beats tanh or SignSwish (KUr5, FCVA), and A's AC required 'further justification'; no one in B raised this core-motivation doubt.
Both committees flagged the missing ReActNet comparison and got the same +0.5 answer; A's AC kept it as a required revision, while B's AC called the rebuttal 'particularly good' and gave an oral.
Neither AC adopted a single reviewer's position; A's AC followed the consensus and B's AC went on its own reading.
B's Reviewer_oG66 raised to 8 'after reading comments from other reviewers', not on new evidence.
No sign that the authors misread or ignored a reviewer on either forum.
B's Reviewer_Xxt6 gave 8 after 2 hours with no stated weakness and posted no note after the rebuttal, and that 8 counted unchallenged toward the oral.
Neither AC set a tier below its reviewers' ratings; A's poster matches 8/7/6.
A's AC stated no assessment above the scores; it leaned on scores without a contrary personal view.
No below-threshold score exists in either committee.
Both committees read the paper as a BNN training method; B's AC added an impact prediction, which is the chair's own reading, not a different contribution type.
All reviewers rated at confidence 4 or 5; none said the core was outside their expertise.
Both committees asked the same things of a methods paper; A's extra justification request is an issue only A raised, not a different bar.
The wrong 'theorem shows rationality' praise occurs on both sides (A's KUr5, B's f6JJ), so it does not separate the committees.
KUr5 said concerns were addressed and kept 7, but that score is above threshold and the definition covers a below-threshold score.
Both committees accepted with rebuttal results; A's AC listed revisions as required changes but did not refuse to credit them.
No reviewer stated a stance at odds with an unedited score that the committee acted on.
B's AC 'separate post' and oG66's cited comments are off-record, but no extra reviewer was called in to break a split.
Clarity was not disputed; all reviewers called the paper clear.
Silent edits by Xxt6 and UYYe have unknown effect and their texts do not argue against acceptance.
No low rating was set aside for silence.
No reviewer in either committee rated above 8, and both had 8s; no champion existed on one side only.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading.
No reviewer contested the premise from a different theoretical school.
B's AC stated a case for the oral (simplicity, predicted impact).
Both committees knew ReActNet and raised it; A's RBNN request is a single missing comparison, not a literature gap.
Neither meta-review misstated reviewers' final positions.
No one raised a narrow-audience concern.
Neither committee had a misreading low-score detractor.
Only B's f6JJ asked for the noise-only row; the authors gave it (77.16) with the ImageNet n_s and f6JJ raised to 7, while A never saw that result.
A's top-confidence reviewer (KUr5, 5) rated 7, below oCAy's 8; no expert review was outweighed.
No late objection entered after the response period.
A's Reviewer_FCVA rated 6 on wholly positive text, while B rated 8/8/8/7 on reviews that mostly restate the paper and are less critical, so part of the gap is scoring leniency.
A's AC asked for further justification of the method's advantage but did not judge a headline claim overstated or require narrowing it.
A's reviewers rated 8/7/6 at confidence 4 to 5, not flat marginal scores from unsure reviewers.

reasoning: Both committees accepted; the oral in B rests on its AC's own reading, taste for a simple idea and an impact prediction no reviewer made (R02), helped by a higher mean from thinner, less critical reviews (R03, R12, R38) and score raises after the rebuttal, one on other reviewers' comments (R06, R10, R35). A alone questioned the core motivation and kept the shared ReActNet weakness as a required revision (R07, R08). The candidate reasons from stage 1 (AC enthusiasm, AC extrapolated impact, unequal score response, thin reviews, motivation challenged on one side, modest gain weighted differently) all map onto existing reasons, so none is added.
